title: Pipes and Directives
summary: Format values in templates with built-in pipes, write a custom pipe, add behaviour to elements with attribute directives and host bindings, and use NgOptimizedImage for images.
introduction: Templates should display data, not reformat it. Pipes take a value and return a display version (a date, a currency, a shortened string) without touching the data itself, and directives attach behaviour and styling to existing elements without wrapping them in a component. This lesson uses the built-in pipes with their exact output, writes a truncate pipe, builds a highlight directive with the host object, and shows why NgOptimizedImage should replace plain img tags.
learningObjectives: Format dates, numbers, currencies and text with built-in pipes and parameters
Write a custom pipe with PipeTransform
Create an attribute directive with inputs and host bindings and use NgOptimizedImage

blocks.text: A pipe sits after a `|` in an expression and transforms the value on its left. Parameters follow after colons. Pipes are standalone classes imported from `@angular/common`, and each one you use must be listed in `imports`. Formatting follows the application's locale, which is `en-US` unless you register another.

blocks.text: The digit pattern `'1.0-1'` reads as *at least 1 integer digit, 0 to 1 decimal digits*. Pipes chain left to right: `{{ issued() | date:'EEEE' | uppercase }}` gives `THURSDAY`.

A pipe is a class with a `transform` method and a `@Pipe` decorator that names it. `ng generate pipe truncate` creates the skeleton. Pipes are **pure** by default: Angular calls `transform` again only when the input value or a parameter changes, which makes them cheaper than calling a method from the template.

blocks.text: A directive is a component without a template: it attaches to an existing element selected by an attribute and changes its behaviour or appearance. Bindings to the host element go in the `host` object of the decorator, with the same `[property]` and `(event)` syntax as a template. Inputs work exactly as in components.

items: `alias: 'appHighlight'` lets the selector attribute double as the input, so `appHighlight="lightblue"` sets the colour.
The `transform` turns the empty string from a bare `appHighlight` attribute back into the default.
Setting the style to `null` removes it, so the paragraph returns to normal when the pointer leaves.
Older code used `@HostBinding` and `@HostListener` decorators for the same thing; the `host` object is the current style and keeps all host interaction in one place.

blocks.title: Common mistake: a directive that is not imported
blocks.text: Forget to add `Highlight` to the component's `imports` and nothing breaks visibly: `appHighlight` becomes an ordinary, meaningless HTML attribute and the hover effect is simply missing. Unknown *elements* raise `NG8001`, but unknown *attributes* are legal HTML, so Angular cannot tell. When a directive seems to do nothing, check the `imports` array first. Binding with brackets, `[appHighlight]="colour()"`, does fail loudly with `NG8002`, which is one argument for the bracket form.

Directives can also inject the element they sit on (`inject(ElementRef)`) for direct DOM access, read other directives on the same element, and be composed with `hostDirectives` so that a component gains a directive's behaviour without the template author adding it. Structural directives, which add or remove elements, are rarely needed now that `@if`, `@for` and `@defer` are built in.

`NgOptimizedImage` is a built-in directive for `` that applies performance best practice automatically: it requires `width` and `height` so the layout never jumps, lazy-loads images that are off screen, marks the most important image with `priority` so the browser fetches it first, and warns in the console when something is wrong. Replace `src` with `ngSrc`.

questions.question: A pure pipe's `transform` runs again on every change detection cycle, even when its input has not changed.
questions.explanation: Pure pipes are memoised: Angular reruns `transform` only when the input value or a parameter changes.
